actions.name: reset_simulation

facts.text: The repository is a simulation library for Agility Robotics' Cassie robot using MuJoCo
cassie_sim_step_pd simulates one step of the Cassie simulator with PD input and state estimator output
The model timestep is 0.0005 s because the controller runs at 2 kHz
The ten actuators are the two legs' hip roll, hip yaw, hip pitch, knee and foot motors, with gear ratios 25, 25, 16, 16 and 50 and ctrlrange +-4.5, +-4.5, +-12.2, +-12.2 and +-0.9 in the motor order
motor() computes the motor-side torque as the output-side torque divided by the actuator gear, clamps it to actuator_ctrlrange and writes data.ctrl

cassie_sim_full_reset copies a 35-element initial qpos and zeroes qvel, ctrl, qfrc_applied, xfrc_applied and qacc, clears the torque delay and reinitializes the state estimator; it does not write the simulator time
The state read-back methods take a slice of the MuJoCo data: qpos is the first nq entries, qvel the first nv entries and ctrl the first nu entries

determinism.notes: MuJoCo is deterministic given the full data state, but CassieSim exposes no full snapshot and full_reset does not clear MuJoCo's warm-start accelerations, so the driver does not claim replay equality; cap.world.reset.v1 records the supplied seed as a label only

gaps: the fake backend is a kinematic stand-in, not MuJoCo: no contacts, gravity, torque-speed limit, state estimator or sensor model; it integrates a placeholder motor response only
full_reset restores the model data, the torque delay and the estimator, but not MuJoCo's warm-start accelerations and not the simulator time; the driver sets the time to zero, so a reset is partial
no physical Cassie is modelled or validated; the UDP interface to a real robot is not bound
the fake's qpos/qvel are the model's array sizes but its inertia and step response are placeholder test data, not the model's dynamics
only the feedforward motor torque is exposed; the pd_in_t task-level and per-motor target and gain inputs are not bound
